sections.h2: Where is Middletown, Connecticut, and how large is it?
sections.html:
Middletown is a city in Middlesex County on the west bank of the Connecticut River, about 16 miles south of Hartford. It had 47,717 residents in the 2020 census and covers 42.36 square miles.

Route 9 runs alongside the river and bisects the city. The west side is flanked by the Metacomet Ridge, including Higby Mountain and the north side of Lamentation Mountain. Middletown shares borders with Cromwell, Portland, East Hampton, Haddam, Durham, Middlefield, Berlin and Meriden.

sections.h2: What is Middletown's history as a river port and mill city?
sections.html:
Middletown began as the Wangunk village of Mattabesset, was settled by English colonists in 1650 and was renamed Middletown in 1653 because it sat roughly halfway along the river. By the American Revolution it was a thriving port, and in the 19th century it became a manufacturing center for marine hardware, typewriters and machine tools.

Wesleyan University was founded in 1831. In 1841, the city established the state's first public high school. In 1868 the Connecticut General Hospital for the Insane opened here, and it is now Connecticut Valley Hospital, still a major employer.

Floods hit the city in 1927 and 1936, and the Great New England Hurricane struck in 1938. A highway built in the 1950s separated the city from the river. Older riverside neighborhoods carry that history, so a seller near the water should expect flood and drainage questions.

sections.h2: Which employers drive Middletown's housing demand?
sections.html:
Middlesex Health Systems is the largest employer, with 3,126 workers, followed by Pratt and Whitney (RTX), per the city's fiscal 2023 financial report as listed on Wikipedia. Health care, aerospace, logistics and education dominate the list.

Wesleyan University and Middlesex Community College are also located in the city. The state's Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection also has its headquarters here, and Middletown holds the Middlesex Superior Court.

Middletown is a patchwork of named areas, from the Main Street downtown near Wesleyan to residential pockets on the west side. The city lists these communities.

  • Highland, the westernmost area and the only part that Interstate 91 crosses.
  • Westfield, a mostly residential area in the northwest corner just south of Cromwell.
  • Miramichi, mostly residential, in the southwest corner.
  • Newfield Heights, a commercial area with many businesses and restaurants north of the center.
  • Bretton Heights, mostly residential, a few miles west of the center.
  • South Farms, mostly residential, just south of the center.
  • Lakeridge Heights, a semi-industrial area, and Maromas, largely industrial, where Pratt and Whitney has an office.

The North End has been the focus of long-running revitalization work, including the 96-unit Wharfside Commons apartments and a community health center that opened in 2012. Whatever the area, the surrounding mix of homes and businesses will influence what a buyer pays.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit connect Middletown?
sections.html:
Route 9 is the spine, and Interstate 91 clips the western edge. River Valley Transit serves Middletown and runs to Old Saybrook, which links to Amtrak and Shore Line East. Connecticut Transit provides local and express service to Hartford and express service to New Haven, and the New Britain Transportation Company connects to New Britain.

  • Bradley International in Windsor Locks and Tweed New Haven are the closest commercial airports.
  • Meriden Markham Airport and Goodspeed Airport in East Haddam handle general aviation.
  • The Arrigoni Bridge, completed in 1938, links the city with Portland across the river.

Schools include Middletown High School, Vinal Technical High School, Xavier High School, Mercy High School and Saint John Paul II Regional Catholic School.

sections.h2: What are Middletown's mill rates and how is the tax computed?
sections.html:
Middletown multiplies the assessment by the mill rate, and the Assessor assesses property at 70% of its value. For the October 1, 2025 grand list, with bills effective July 1, 2026, the city's combined real estate rate is 40.800 mills in the City Fire District, 38.611 in the South Fire District and 35.384 in the Westfield Fire District.

District (Oct. 1, 2025 grand list)City mill rateFire districtCombined
City Fire District33.307.5040.800
South Fire District33.305.31138.611
Westfield Fire District33.302.08435.384

As an illustration only, a house valued at $300,000 would be assessed at $210,000, and 40.800 mills on that comes to about $8,568 a year. The registered vehicle rate is capped at 32.46. Check the mill rates page for current numbers.

The City Fire District tax is added to the city bill, while the South Fire and Westfield Fire Districts bill and collect separately, so an owner in those districts should expect two bills.

sections.h2: When is Middletown property tax due, and who gets the bill?
sections.html:
Middletown's real estate tax covers the fiscal year of July 1 through June 30 and is due in two installments, July 1 and January 1. Tax not paid by the first business day of the month after the due date carries interest of 1.5% per month, or 18% per year, from the due date on the unpaid installment.

  • Not getting a bill does not cancel the tax or the interest, and copies are free.
  • Banks and mortgage companies that escrow must request bills each year from the Tax Collector.
  • Bills go to the record owner as of the October 1 grand list date, and by law that name stays on the bill until the next assessment date.
  • If you pay off a mortgage, tell the office so it can update its records.

After a sale, the bill can therefore still show the earlier owner, so confirm with the collector who receives it. The tax collector's page is here.

sections.h2: How do you sell a Middletown house with tax owed?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff, then let the title company pay it from the proceeds at closing. The Middletown town clerk records the deed, and the state conveyance tax return, Form OP-236, is filed at that time. Middletown's code on the Department of Revenue Services list is 083.

The state lists exemptions for a principal residence given in lieu of foreclosure and for one whose price does not cover the mortgages plus the priority tax liens. See the state page.

Cash Home Buyers buys Middletown houses as-is, whether the owner is behind on tax, inherited the property or lives out of state.

faqs.q: When are Middletown real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: July 1 and January 1. Interest of 1.5% per month applies if an installment is not paid by the first business day of the following month.
The Assessor assesses property at 70% of its value, and the city multiplies that assessment by the mill rate.

faqs.q: What is the Middletown mill rate?
faqs.a: For the October 1, 2025 grand list, the city lists 40.800 mills in the City Fire District, 38.611 in the South Fire District and 35.384 in the Westfield Fire District.

faqs.q: Do some Middletown owners get two tax bills?
faqs.a: Yes. South Fire and Westfield Fire District owners are billed and collected separately by those districts.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Middletown house if I owe tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company normally pays the tax from your sale proceeds at closing.
Middletown's probate court district covers the city plus Cromwell, Portland, Middlefield and Haddam, which matters if you are selling an inherited house.

faqs.q: Whose name is on a Middletown tax bill after a sale?
faqs.a: The record owner as of the October 1 grand list date stays on the bill until the next assessment date.
